messages.subject: Re: How to help users with install issues?
messages.subject_clean: How to help users with install issues?
messages.body_plain:
The best way in general is to get your package on cran. This is painful, obviously, but does avoid many potential installation problems.

Hadley

On Friday, January 31, 2014, <arila...@gmail.com> wrote:

> A few weeks ago I was thrilled to be able to share my R package with people via github thru the help of devtools.  Now I am in a new position: some people cannot run my examples, and I am not sure how to help them.  For reference:
>
> Here is my project: https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr
> Here is my forum for people to report problems: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/choroplethr
>
> The first two issues were resolved by asking people to upgrade their version of R from 2.15 to 3.0.2.  However, now someone has reported an issue with 3.0.2:
>
> https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/choroplethr/ixFezN2EG8U
>
> I began following up by asking him to clarify what OS he is using since I didn't immediately recognize it.  Once I have that I am planning to try to get a machine with that OS that I can then try to debug locally.
>
> I'm wondering though: is there a standard list of Q&A that people normally run thru when they try to help people remotely with their packages?  I'm basically just making this up as I go along, and was wondering if there is a better way.
>
> Thanks.
>
> Ari
>

messages.subject: how to use only data from another package
messages.subject_clean: how to use only data from another package
messages.body_plain:
I just released my package <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/choroplethr/index.html> on cran and users are reporting a problem that I am now able to reproduce.  It has to do with Imports vs. Suggets vs. Depends.  You can see my DESCRIPTION file here <https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr/blob/master/DESCRIPTION>, and I'll reproduce the important parts below

Imports:
    ggplot2,
Suggests:
    maps,
    zipcode

The reason that I put maps and zipcode in Suggets and not Imports is because R CMD generates this NOTE which prevented acceptance by CRAN:

* checking dependencies in R code ... NOTE
Namespaces in Imports field not imported from:
  ‘maps’ ‘zipcode’
  All declared Imports should be used.
See the information on DESCRIPTION files in the chapter ‘Creating R
packages’ of the ‘Writing R Extensions’ manual.

While it's true that my NAMESPACE file does not mention these packages, I do load data from them.  For example, see this line in my file county.R <https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr/blob/master/R/county.R>

  data(county.fips, package="maps", envir = environment())

So if someone does not have the maps package installed, it looks like installing my package will not install it for them, and then they get an error as soon as they hit this line.

So then the question becomes: how can I references this data in the NAMESPACE file so that R CMD CHECK is happy?  I tried to add this roxygen line:

#' @importFrom maps county.fips

But then my application fails to build with this error:

** preparing package for lazy loading
Error : object ‘county.fips’ is not exported by 'namespace:maps'
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package ‘choroplethr’

And if you look at the NAMESPACE file for maps you can see that this is true.

Does anyone have advice on how to proceed?

Thanks.

Ari

messages.body_plain:
You know, I considered that.  That solution reminds of how they required me to add code like this in every file where I use ggplot2:

(base::getRversion() >= "2.15.1") {
  utils::globalVariables(c(...))
}

We had some back and forth about this, but they insisted I add it.  (See this <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9439256/how-can-i-handle-r-cmd-check-no-visible-binding-for-global-variable-notes-when> stackoverflow for a larger discussion about this problem).

Overall, I feel that adding code to my project to satisfy "notes" from an automated program lowers the quality of my project.  But if enough users mention the problem that my dependency declaration causes I'll consider doing this.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
Just started seeing two errors, perhaps since updating roxygen2 to 3.1.0. (which by the way reports itself as packageVersion("roxygen") # -> 0.1.3

My package "umx" will still document() and install() without error. But when I run_examples(), I get this error...

> devtools::run_examples("~/bin/umx")
Updating umx documentation
Updating namespace directives
Error in stop(..., srcref_location(srcref), call. = FALSE) :
  Roclet processing error in block fit_and_reporting.r:1058
Missing name in block fit_and_reporting.r:1058

I can't see anything wrong around that line (and nothing has changed.

Secondly, some functions with #' export in their roxygen are no longer exporting.

umx::print.dataframe
Error: 'print.dataframe' is not an exported object from 'namespace:umx'

despite this being the (unchanged) roxy code ahead of the function

Any clues?
